report.executive_summary: A 46-month P&C portfolio of 1,300 policies across Auto and Home lines has earned $4,023,883.78 in premium with a 60.5% loss ratio and $2,433,528.68 in incurred losses. Auto is the larger line by both premium and losses, while the overall loss ratio of 60.5% reflects case-incurred losses only, with no IBNR, meaning 2025 and 2026 results are still developing and not yet comparable to earlier years. Earned Premium dropped sharply month-over-month in Sep 2026 versus Aug 2026, and 178 Renewal Status records were unreadable and grouped as 'Unknown', which may affect retention analysis.

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as P&C insurance data (earned premium, loss ratio, incurred losses, policies, claims, severity (incurred per claim), written premium, retention rate, average written premium per term). Losses are reported (case-incurred: paid to date plus case reserves) as of the latest valuation, with no IBNR and no loss-adjustment expense, in nominal dollars with no trend applied; loss ratios use earned premium. Lines differ in mix and exposure units, so a total across lines is a mix of them. Oct 2026 is partial (data through the 26th) and is left out of period comparisons. The data has no valuation date; measured to its last date (26 Oct 2026), 2026 (10 months) and 2025 (22 months) are still developing: their losses will usually rise, so they are not final and not comparable with mature years. Gender is shown as a description only: rating or underwriting on sex is restricted or banned in several US states (NAIC Model 880, Colorado SB21-169), so no rate recommendation is made on it.

executive_view.headline: A 46-month P&C portfolio of 1,300 policies across Auto and Home lines has earned $4,023,883.78 in premium with a 60.5% loss ratio and $2,433,528.68 in incurred losses.

paragraphs.text: Auto is the larger line by both premium and losses, while the overall loss ratio of 60.5% reflects case-incurred losses only, with no IBNR, meaning 2025 and 2026 results are still developing and not yet comparable to earlier years.
Earned Premium dropped sharply month-over-month in Sep 2026 versus Aug 2026, and 178 Renewal Status records were unreadable and grouped as 'Unknown', which may affect retention analysis.

findings.text: Auto accounts for $2,617,354.01 in earned premium and $1,448,019.65 in incurred losses; Home accounts for $1,406,529.77 in earned premium and $985,509.03 in incurred losses — Auto is the dominant line on both measures.

Incurred losses are highly concentrated: the median policy shows $0 in losses while the mean is $910.07 and the maximum reaches $96,357.19, indicating that a small number of claims drive the bulk of total losses.
Earned Premium ranges from -$3,958.90 to $8,052.87 per policy, with a median of $1,415.89; negative values suggest mid-term cancellations or endorsements and warrant a closer review.
Earned Premium fell in Sep 2026 compared with Aug 2026, a month-over-month move that may partly reflect the partial October cut-off rather than an underlying business shift.
